events.description: Senator Tom Cotton's New York Times op-ed 'Send in the Troops' called for deploying the military to restore order.
US-Taliban withdrawal deal signed in Doha.
Mullah Mansour was formally named Taliban emir overall; Zawahiri pledged allegiance and Mansour publicly accepted it in a speech, later taken down.
Mullah Mansour was killed by the Obama administration in Pakistan.
Suhail Shaheen told CBS News he was unsure that bin Laden and al-Qaeda were behind 9/11.
Per the UN report, Hamza bin Laden met a Taliban delegation in spring 2019 and received assurances that the Taliban would not betray al-Qaeda.
The White House announced Hamza bin Laden was dead, without giving place or date and saying only 'Afghanistan, Pakistan region'.
Raid in Helmand (Musa Qala) in which Asim Umar was killed with his courier; al-Qaeda was being harbored by the Taliban.
Per the UN report, Zawahiri met an Akani delegation (incl. Yahya Haqqani) and received assurances; location unknown.
The UN Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team released a report alleging ongoing Taliban-al-Qaeda ties, thousands of Pakistani fighters, and possible Haqqani-ISKP accommodation.

key_claims: The hosts argue the Taliban has not publicly disavowed al-Qaeda or rejected Zawahiri's pledge to Akhundzada, which they see as an easy first step.
They say Mullah Mansour publicly accepted Zawahiri's allegiance in 2015, and that the Taliban removed the speech after Long War Journal reported it.
The UN report says Hamza bin Laden met a Taliban delegation in spring 2019 for assurances that the Taliban would not betray al-Qaeda.
The UN report says Zawahiri met a Haqqani delegation including Yahya Haqqani, Sirajuddin's brother-in-law, in February 2020, before the Doha deal.
The hosts say the Taliban-al-Qaeda relationship is personal as well as institutional, involving intermarriage and al-Qaeda embedded in Taliban training and religious indoctrination.
The hosts say 6,000-6,500 Pakistani fighters from LeT, JeM and TTP operate in Afghanistan under Taliban protection, and the real number is probably higher.
The hosts theorize, without proof, that the Haqqani Network and Taliban tolerate ISKP attacks in Kabul because they help delegitimize the Afghan government.
The hosts say U.S. officials have not denied or publicized the report's findings because they conflict with the push to withdraw.
The UN report says some ISKP attacks in Kabul may stem from a tactical accommodation with the Haqqani Network.
Many ISKP members were formerly Afghan Taliban, Pakistani Taliban, al-Qaeda or IMU, so ties persist at the local level.
ISKP drew commanders and facilitators from the Kabul attack network that included the Haqqanis and al-Qaeda.
The Haqqani Network is a Pakistani state asset, so ISI direction of attacks is plausible though unproven.
Hosts say intelligence officials from two other countries told them of Taliban complicity, which they cannot verify.
